answer: Give each agent a telemetry heartbeat identity. It registers one device fingerprint, sensor noise and clock skew, and posts a 500-token bond. Every epoch it signs a heartbeat with fresh noise samples only that hardware makes. Verifiers compare fingerprints and burn the bond of any two matching within 0.1 percent. A heartbeat over 90 seconds late marks the identity dormant. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 boards at $35 each: $35,000 in hardware plus $12,000 a year in power. A sybil farm is a vine trying to climb a knoll and a ridge at once: one stem, one slope, and the extra shoots wither.
